headline: Markets Close Friday on a Broad Rally, but Geopolitical Friction and a Looming Earnings Giant Keep Traders Cautious Into the New Week
body_html:
Equities finished Friday's session on constructive footing, with advancing issues outpacing decliners by more than two to one across the 550-name universe — 370 up against 176 down. Materials led all sectors with a gain of 1.48%, propelled in part by a sharp 8.09% surge in Alpha Metallurgical Resources and a 6.75% advance in lithium specialist Albemarle. Homebuilders added 1.14%, Software rose 0.98%, and Healthcare tacked on 0.94%, giving the session a notably defensive-yet-cyclical complexion. Semiconductors were the lone sector in the red, slipping 0.23% as Marvell Technology shed 5.57% to head the decliner board.

Underpinning the cautious tone was a week defined by rising tension in the Strait of Hormuz. Reports that Iranian authorities permitted a selection of Iraqi oil tankers passage through the waterway did little to dull concerns; NATO members were separately reported to be weighing options around the strait outside formal alliance channels, while US-Iran rhetoric remained pointed ahead of a fresh round of American sanctions. Bond yields stayed in focus throughout, and Wall Street, despite Friday's recovery, finished the full week lower.

The calendar ahead is dense. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is scheduled to hold a press conference Monday — a session that investors will parse closely after Ray Dalio publicly linked a similar policy signal to growing risks of a sovereign debt crisis, recommending gold and bitcoin as hedges. A closely watched artificial-intelligence bellwether also faces earnings scrutiny, with commentary on data-center demand expected to set the tone for the semiconductor complex early in the week.

briefs.headline: Bessent Press Conference Sets Monday's Agenda
briefs.body: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is set to address reporters Monday, drawing immediate market attention. The appearance comes after hedge-fund veteran Ray Dalio argued that signaling from the Treasury is symptomatic of a debt crisis drawing nearer, a comment that lifted safe-haven interest in gold and digital assets heading into the weekend.

briefs.headline: Dalio Flags Debt-Crisis Risk, Pivots to Hard Assets
briefs.body: Bridgewater founder Ray Dalio went on record warning that recent fiscal policy moves bring a sovereign debt reckoning closer, singling out gold and bitcoin as preferred stores of value. The remarks reverberated across macro desks Friday and are likely to sharpen focus on Monday's Bessent briefing for any rebuttal or clarification.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Passage Granted but Tensions Show No Sign of Easing
briefs.body: Iran permitted a number of Iraqi oil tankers to transit the Strait of Hormuz, according to Reuters, yet the geopolitical backdrop remained fraught. Washington and Tehran continued to exchange hostile language ahead of new US sanctions, and a separate report detailed an Iran-linked tanker falling victim to a resurgent wave of Somali piracy.

briefs.headline: NATO Allies Weigh Hormuz Options Outside Alliance Framework
briefs.body: Member states of the North Atlantic alliance held discussions over potential responses to Strait of Hormuz disruptions, though deliberations are proceeding without formal NATO involvement, Reuters reported. The development underscores the extent to which the waterway has become a focal point for energy-security planners as US-Iran friction intensifies.

briefs.headline: Citadel Slashes Exposure in Situational Awareness Book
briefs.body: Ken Griffin disclosed that Citadel has unwound more than 80% of the risk associated with its Situational Awareness portfolio, a notable de-risking move from one of the industry's largest multi-strategy platforms. The disclosure adds to a broader picture of institutional caution heading into a week packed with policy events and high-profile earnings.

briefs.headline: AI Earnings Loom Large for Semiconductor Sector
briefs.body: A pivotal artificial-intelligence chipmaker is set to report results in the coming week, with analysts flagging the print as a critical read on data-center spending momentum. The semiconductor sector was Friday's lone decliner, slipping 0.23%, and commentary on forward demand could determine whether that underperformance deepens or reverses sharply.
